name: comp-57

frames.best_why: Three tag chips fill the focused strip beside the Add a tag placeholder, showing the full pattern.

tagline: Type a word, press enter, and it becomes a removable chip inside the field.
summary: A wide single-line field that holds several small outlined labels, each with its own cross, alongside a muted placeholder for adding another. Typing and confirming grows the row of chips.
appearance: A long rounded strip with a thin border sits on a dark stage, filled left to right by small rounded chips carrying short words and a tiny cross, ending in faint "Add a tag" placeholder text. A small label floats above and a dim credit line sits below.
behaviour: Typing a word and confirming turns it into a chip that pushes the placeholder to the right; the whole strip gains a ring while focused. Hovering a chip and clicking its cross removes it, and the row reflows.
demo_content: Label "Input with inner tags", tags Red, Design and Motion, placeholder "Add a tag", credit "Built with emblor".
search_phrases: add multiple tags in one field
type and press enter to add tag
use_when: People need to attach several short labels, keywords or recipients to one record while keeping them all visible.
avoid_when: It pulls in the emblor library, and the starting tag and vendor credit line are baked into the demo file.
customise: The wrapper exposes no props; starting tags, placeholder and chip styling are set through TagInput inside the file, so new content means editing it.
weight_why: A few chips and one input, with transitions only on hover and focus.

a11y.note: Label and focus ring are wired up, but chip remove buttons depend on the library for names and no reduced-motion check exists.

polish_why: A competent stock tag field; plain chips and a vendor credit line keep it ordinary.
title: Inline Tags Input
